requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"

module VERIFICATION
  imports MPY

  // Explicit form of Map deletion used by function-frame teardown.
  rule (((X:KItem |-> _:KItem) M:Map) [ X <- undef ]) => M
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
       [simplification]
  rule (M:Map [ X:KItem <- V:KItem ]) => (X |-> V) M
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
       [simplification]

  // Proof-normalization lemmas for ordinary (non-closure-cell) frames.  These
  // are guarded specializations of MPY's existing rules; the priority prevents
  // the symbolic prover from exploring impossible cellRef branches after the
  // guard has established that "$cells" is absent.
  rule <k> Name(X:String) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys(M))
       [priority(39)]

  rule <k> Name(X:String) => V:Val ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((X |-> V) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool ("$cells" in_keys(M))
       [priority(39)]

  // Direct literal cooling, equivalent to Int(I) => I followed by Assign's
  // strictness context.  Keeping it explicit avoids a symbolic freezer branch
  // at loop-summary boundaries.
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), Int(I:Int)) => Assign(Name(X), I) ... </k>
       [priority(39)]

  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), Bool(B:Bool)) => Assign(Name(X), B) ... </k>
       [priority(39)]

  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(
         ((X |-> _:Val) M:Map => (X |-> V) M),
         _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(
         M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ],
         _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(39)]

  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(
         ((X |-> A:Val) M:Map => (X |-> applyBin(OP, A, V)) M),
         _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> A) M))
         andBool notBool isRefV(A)
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> #bindTgt(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool ("$cells" in_keys(M))
       [priority(39)]

  rule <k> #bindTgt(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(
         ((X |-> _:Val) M:Map => (X |-> V) M),
         _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  // Strictness-normalized forms used by the outer list loop.
  rule <k> Compare(Name(X:String), CmpOp(OP:String, Name(Y:String)))
        => applyCmp(OP, A, B) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(
         (X |-> A:Val) (Y |-> B:Val) M:Map,
         _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X =/=String Y
         andBool notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool (Y in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> A) (Y |-> B) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> Compare(Name(X:String), CmpOp(OP:String, Int(I:Int)))
        => applyCmp(OP, A, I) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((X |-> A:Val) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> A) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> If(Name(X:String), T:Stmts, E:Stmts)
        => #branch(truthy(V), T, E) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((X |-> V:Val) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), Name(Y:String))
        => Assign(Name(X), V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((Y |-> V:Val) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (Y in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((Y |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> Return(Name(X:String)) => Return(V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((X |-> V:Val) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k> For(T:Expr, Name(X:String), B:Stmts)
        => #loop(V, T, B) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope((X |-> V:Val) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys((X |-> V) M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k>
         Call(
           Name("skjkasdkd"),
           (list(asVals(IS:IntList)), .Exprs))
        => #applyK(
             toCall(closureVal(
               ("lst", .ParamNames),
               #functionBody,
               0)),
             (list(asVals(IS)), .Vals)) ...
       </k>
       <env> 0 </env>
       <scopes>
         ... 0 |-> scope(
           ("skjkasdkd" |-> closureVal(
             ("lst", .ParamNames),
             #functionBody,
             0))
           M:Map,
           parent(-1)) ...
       </scopes>
       requires notBool ("skjkasdkd" in_keys(M))
       [priority(38)]

  rule <k>
         Assign(
           Name("prime"),
           Compare(Name("number"), CmpOp(">=", Int(2))))
        => Assign(Name("prime"), N >=Int 2) ...
       </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(("number" |-> N:Int) M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool ("number" in_keys(M))
         andBool notBool ("$cells" in_keys(("number" |-> N) M))
       [priority(38)]

  // Integer-only input lists.  This sort makes the task's stated input
  // precondition structural, so symbolic execution never admits a non-int
  // element.
  syntax IntList ::= ".IntList" | intCons(Int, IntList)

  syntax ValSeq ::= asVals(IntList)

  // Structural iterator cases expose IntList's constructors to narrowing.
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(asVals(.IntList))) => #iterDone ... </k>
       [priority(39)]
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(asVals(intCons(I:Int, IS:IntList))))
        => #iterYield(I, list(asVals(IS))) ... </k>
       [priority(39)]

  // The mathematical primality oracle follows the implementation's trial
  // division exactly.  false means that an earlier divisor was already found.
  syntax Bool ::= trialPrime(Int, Int, Bool) [function, total]
  rule trialPrime(_:Int, _:Int, false) => false
  rule trialPrime(N:Int, D:Int, true) => true
    requires D *Int D >Int N
  rule trialPrime(N:Int, D:Int, true) => false
    requires D *Int D <=Int N andBool pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0
    [simplification]
  rule trialPrime(N:Int, D:Int, true) => trialPrime(N, D +Int 1, true)
    requires D *Int D <=Int N
      andBool notBool (pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0)
    [simplification]

  // The final divisor value is specified too, allowing the loop invariant to
  // describe the whole local store rather than hiding a side effect.
  syntax Int ::= trialDivisor(Int, Int, Bool) [function, total]
  rule trialDivisor(_:Int, D:Int, false) => D
  rule trialDivisor(N:Int, D:Int, true) => D
    requires D *Int D >Int N
  rule trialDivisor(N:Int, D:Int, true) => D +Int 1
    requires D *Int D <=Int N andBool pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0
    [simplification]
  rule trialDivisor(N:Int, D:Int, true)
    => trialDivisor(N, D +Int 1, true)
    requires D *Int D <=Int N
      andBool notBool (pyMod(N, D) ==Int 0)
    [simplification]

  syntax Bool ::= isPrime(Int) [function, total]
  rule isPrime(N:Int) => trialPrime(N, 2, N >=Int 2)

  syntax Int ::= largestPrime(IntList, Int) [function, total]
  rule largestPrime(.IntList, CUR:Int) => CUR
  rule largestPrime(intCons(N:Int, IS:IntList), CUR:Int)
    => largestPrime(IS, N)
    requires N >Int CUR andBool isPrime(N)
    [simplification]
  rule largestPrime(intCons(N:Int, IS:IntList), CUR:Int)
    => largestPrime(IS, CUR)
    requires N <=Int CUR
      orBool (N >Int CUR andBool notBool isPrime(N))
    [simplification]

  syntax Int ::= digitAcc(Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule digitAcc(N:Int, A:Int) => A
    requires N <=Int 0
    [simplification]
  rule digitAcc(N:Int, A:Int)
    => digitAcc(
         (N -Int pyMod(N, 10)) /Int 10,
         A +Int pyMod(N, 10))
    requires N >Int 0
    [simplification]

  syntax Int ::= digitSum(Int) [function, total]
  rule digitSum(N:Int) => digitAcc(N, 0)

  // Exact AST fragments emitted by py2mpy.py for solution.py.
  syntax Expr ::= "#primeCond" [macro]
  rule #primeCond => BoolOp(
    "and",
    Name("prime"),
    Compare(
      BinOp("*", Name("divisor"), Name("divisor")),
      CmpOp("<=", Name("number"))))

  syntax Stmts ::= "#primeBody" [macro]
  rule #primeBody =>
    If(Compare(
      BinOp("%", Name("number"), Name("divisor")),
      CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
      Assign(Name("prime"), Bool(false)),
      .Stmts)
    AugAssign(Name("divisor"), "+", Int(1))

  syntax Stmts ::= "#scanBody" [macro]
  rule #scanBody =>
    If(Compare(Name("number"), CmpOp(">", Name("largest"))),
      Assign(Name("divisor"), Int(2))
      Assign(
        Name("prime"),
        Compare(Name("number"), CmpOp(">=", Int(2))))
      While(#primeCond, #primeBody)
      If(Name("prime"),
        Assign(Name("largest"), Name("number")),
        .Stmts),
      .Stmts)

  syntax Expr ::= "#digitCond" [macro]
  rule #digitCond =>
    Compare(Name("largest"), CmpOp(">", Int(0)))

  syntax Stmts ::= "#digitBody" [macro]
  rule #digitBody =>
    AugAssign(
      Name("digit_total"),
      "+",
      BinOp("%", Name("largest"), Int(10)))
    AugAssign(Name("largest"), "//", Int(10))

  syntax Stmts ::= "#functionBody" [macro]
  rule #functionBody =>
    Assign(Name("largest"), Int(0))
    Assign(Name("number"), Int(0))
    Assign(Name("divisor"), Int(2))
    Assign(Name("prime"), Bool(false))
    Assign(Name("digit_total"), Int(0))
    For(Name("number"), Name("lst"), #scanBody)
    While(#digitCond, #digitBody)
    Return(Name("digit_total"))

  // Bounded entry-prefix summary.  It is the direct composition of MPY-CALL's
  // frame allocation, #bindP, the five literal assignments, and For's
  // one-time iterable evaluation.  No loop iteration is summarized here.
  rule <k>
         #applyK(
           toCall(closureVal(
             ("lst", .ParamNames),
             #functionBody,
             0)),
           (list(asVals(IS:IntList)), .Vals))
        =>
         #loop(list(asVals(IS)), Name("number"), #scanBody)
         ~> While(#digitCond, #digitBody)
         ~> Return(Name("digit_total"))
         ~> #endcall
       </k>
       <env> 0 => 1 </env>
       <scopes>
         MOD:Map
         =>
         MOD
         1 |-> scope(
           ("lst" |-> list(asVals(IS)))
           ("largest" |-> 0)
           ("number" |-> 0)
           ("divisor" |-> 2)
           ("prime" |-> false)
           ("digit_total" |-> 0),
           parent(0))
       </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> 1 => 2 </scopeLoc>
       <stack>
         .List => ListItem(frame(.K, 0, 1))
       </stack>
       requires notBool (1 in_keys(MOD))
       [priority(37)]

  syntax Module ::= "solutionModule" [macro]
  rule solutionModule =>
    Module(FuncDef("skjkasdkd", Params("lst"), #functionBody))
endmodule

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# The required translation artifact.
python3 py2mpy.py solution.py > solution.mpy

# Concrete LLVM execution: the six prompt examples and four edge cases are
# assertions in concrete-tests.py.
python3 - <<'PY'
import ast

def first_function(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as source:
        tree = ast.parse(source.read(), filename=path)
    return next(node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef))

assert ast.dump(first_function("solution.py")) == ast.dump(first_function("concrete-tests.py"))
PY
python3 py2mpy.py concrete-tests.py > concrete-tests.mpy
kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k \
  --backend llvm \
  --main-module MPY-KRUN \
  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
  --output-definition runtime-kompiled
krun concrete-tests.mpy --definition runtime-kompiled

# Symbolic definition: VERIFICATION imports MPY, never MPY-CONCRETE.
kompile verification.k \
  --backend haskell \
  --main-module VERIFICATION \
  --syntax-module VERIFICATION \
  --output-definition verification-kompiled \
  -I .

# Prove each invariant before admitting it as a trusted dependency of a later
# modular proof command.
kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC \
  --claims SPEC.prime-loop \
  --output pretty

kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC \
  --claims SPEC.digit-loop \
  --output pretty

kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC \
  --claims SPEC.scan-loop,SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --trusted SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --output pretty

kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC \
  --claims SPEC.entry-prefix,SPEC.scan-loop,SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --trusted SPEC.scan-loop,SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --output pretty

kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module SPEC \
  --claims SPEC.main-correct,SPEC.entry-prefix,SPEC.scan-loop,SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --trusted SPEC.entry-prefix,SPEC.scan-loop,SPEC.prime-loop,SPEC.digit-loop \
  --output pretty

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent differential test for the trusted and generated entry points."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import itertools
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path


TRUSTED = Path("/tmp/audit-work/trusted/canonical.py")
GENERATED = Path("/tmp/audit-work/reconstruction/solution.py")
INPUT_RECORD = Path("/audit-output/evidence/stage2/differential-inputs.json")


def load_entry(path: Path, module_name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"cannot import {path}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.skjkasdkd


def mathematical_result(values: list[int]) -> int:
    """Direct oracle for the natural-language 'largest prime' contract."""

    def is_prime(value: int) -> bool:
        if value < 2:
            return False
        divisor = 2
        while divisor * divisor <= value:
            if value % divisor == 0:
                return False
            divisor += 1
        return True

    largest = max((value for value in values if is_prime(value)), default=0)
    return sum(int(character) for character in str(largest))


DOCUMENTED = [
    [0, 3, 2, 1, 3, 5, 7, 4, 5, 5, 5, 2, 181, 32, 4, 32, 3, 2, 32, 324, 4, 3],
    [1, 0, 1, 8, 2, 4597, 2, 1, 3, 40, 1, 2, 1, 2, 4, 2, 5, 1],
    [1, 3, 1, 32, 5107, 34, 83278, 109, 163, 23, 2323, 32, 30, 1, 9, 3],
    [0, 724, 32, 71, 99, 32, 6, 0, 5, 91, 83, 0, 5, 6],
    [0, 81, 12, 3, 1, 21],
    [0, 8, 1, 2, 1, 7],
]

BOUNDARIES = {
    "empty": [],
    "negative_zero_only": [-5, -1, 0],
    "one_only": [1],
    "zero_and_one": [0, 1, 0],
    "prime_cutoff_two": [2],
    "outer_equal_and_lower": [2, 2, 1],
    "outer_greater_composite_then_prime": [4, 2],
    "trial_loop_not_entered_at_three": [3],
    "trial_loop_enters_and_divides_at_four": [4],
    "trial_loop_enters_nondividing_at_five": [5],
    "later_divisor_at_nine": [9],
    "square_of_prime": [49],
    "later_larger_prime": [5, 11],
    "later_smaller_prime": [11, 5],
    "digit_zero_inside_prime": [101],
    "multi_digit_prime": [997],
    "mixed_signs_and_primes": [-7, 0, 1, 2, 17, 16],
}


def invoke(function, values):
    try:
        return ("value", function(list(values)))
    except Exception as error:  # preserve divergences in exception behavior
        return ("exception", type(error).__name__, str(error))


def main() -> int:
    canonical = load_entry(TRUSTED, "trusted_canonical")
    generated = load_entry(GENERATED, "generated_solution")

    tagged_cases: list[tuple[str, list[int]]] = []
    tagged_cases.extend((f"documented_{index + 1}", case) for index, case in enumerate(DOCUMENTED))
    tagged_cases.extend((f"boundary_{name}", case) for name, case in BOUNDARIES.items())

    alphabet = [-3, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11, 25]
    for length in range(4):
        for values in itertools.product(alphabet, repeat=length):
            tagged_cases.append((f"exhaustive_len_{length}", list(values)))

    rng = random.Random(940094)
    for index in range(500):
        length = rng.randrange(0, 11)
        values = [rng.randrange(-50, 5001) for _ in range(length)]
        tagged_cases.append((f"generated_{index}", values))

    INPUT_RECORD.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "documented": DOCUMENTED,
                "boundaries": BOUNDARIES,
                "exhaustive_alphabet": alphabet,
                "exhaustive_lengths": [0, 1, 2, 3],
                "random_seed": 940094,
                "random_case_count": 500,
                "random_value_range": [-50, 5000],
                "random_length_range": [0, 10],
                "expanded_cases": tagged_cases,
            },
            indent=2,
            sort_keys=True,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    candidate_canonical_mismatches = []
    candidate_oracle_mismatches = []
    canonical_oracle_mismatches = []
    for label, values in tagged_cases:
        candidate_result = invoke(generated, values)
        canonical_result = invoke(canonical, values)
        oracle_result = ("value", mathematical_result(values))
        if candidate_result != canonical_result:
            candidate_canonical_mismatches.append(
                (label, values, candidate_result, canonical_result)
            )
        if candidate_result != oracle_result:
            candidate_oracle_mismatches.append(
                (label, values, candidate_result, oracle_result)
            )
        if canonical_result != oracle_result:
            canonical_oracle_mismatches.append(
                (label, values, canonical_result, oracle_result)
            )

    print(f"total_cases={len(tagged_cases)}")
    print(f"candidate_vs_canonical_mismatches={len(candidate_canonical_mismatches)}")
    print(f"candidate_vs_math_oracle_mismatches={len(candidate_oracle_mismatches)}")
    print(f"canonical_vs_math_oracle_mismatches={len(canonical_oracle_mismatches)}")
    print("first_candidate_vs_canonical_mismatches:")
    for mismatch in candidate_canonical_mismatches[:30]:
        print(repr(mismatch))
    print("first_candidate_vs_math_oracle_mismatches:")
    for mismatch in candidate_oracle_mismatches[:30]:
        print(repr(mismatch))

    # Candidate/canonical disagreements remain evidence, but the natural-
    # language oracle determines whether the generated implementation is wrong.
    return 1 if candidate_oracle_mismatches else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lexically inventory K sentences for the audit's exhaustive static review."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path("/tmp/audit-work/reconstruction")
OUTPUT_JSON = Path("/audit-output/evidence/stage5/rule-inventory.json")
OUTPUT_MD = Path("/audit-output/evidence/stage5/rule-inventory.md")

START = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(requires|module|endmodule|imports|configuration|"
    r"context(?:\s+alias)?|syntax|rule|claim)\b"
)


def classify(text: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    first = text.lstrip().split(None, 1)[0]
    tags: list[str] = []
    if first == "syntax":
        kind = "syntax"
        for tag in (
            "function",
            "total",
            "functional",
            "macro",
            "hook",
            "token",
            "symbol",
            "bracket",
        ):
            if re.search(rf"\b{tag}\b", text):
                tags.append(tag)
    elif first == "rule":
        kind = "rule"
        tags.append("simplification" if "simplification" in text else "ordinary")
        if "priority(" in text:
            tags.append("priority")
        if "owise" in text:
            tags.append("owise")
        if "anywhere" in text:
            tags.append("anywhere")
    elif first == "claim":
        kind = "claim"
        if "trusted" in text:
            tags.append("trusted")
    else:
        kind = first
    return kind, tags


def sentences(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    result: list[dict] = []
    active_start: int | None = None
    active_lines: list[str] = []

    def finish() -> None:
        nonlocal active_start, active_lines
        if active_start is None:
            return
        text = "\n".join(active_lines).rstrip()
        kind, tags = classify(text)
        result.append(
            {
                "file": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
                "line": active_start,
                "kind": kind,
                "tags": tags,
                "text": text,
            }
        )
        active_start = None
        active_lines = []

    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        stripped = line.lstrip()
        if stripped.startswith("//") or not stripped:
            if active_start is not None:
                active_lines.append(line)
            continue
        if START.match(line):
            finish()
            active_start = number
            active_lines = [line]
        elif active_start is not None:
            active_lines.append(line)
    finish()
    return result


def main() -> None:
    paths = sorted((ROOT / "reference-semantics").rglob("*.k"))
    paths.extend([ROOT / "verification.k", ROOT / "spec.k"])
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        records.extend(sentences(path))

    counts = Counter(record["kind"] for record in records)
    rule_tags = Counter(
        tag
        for record in records
        if record["kind"] == "rule"
        for tag in record["tags"]
    )
    syntax_tags = Counter(
        tag
        for record in records
        if record["kind"] == "syntax"
        for tag in record["tags"]
    )
    payload = {
        "source_root": str(ROOT),
        "files": [str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) for path in paths],
        "counts": dict(sorted(counts.items())),
        "rule_tags": dict(sorted(rule_tags.items())),
        "syntax_tags": dict(sorted(syntax_tags.items())),
        "records": records,
    }
    OUTPUT_JSON.write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )

    rows = [
        "# Exhaustive lexical K inventory",
        "",
        f"Source root: `{ROOT}`",
        "",
        f"Files: {len(paths)}; records: {len(records)}",
        "",
        f"Sentence counts: `{dict(sorted(counts.items()))}`",
        "",
        f"Rule tags: `{dict(sorted(rule_tags.items()))}`",
        "",
        f"Syntax tags: `{dict(sorted(syntax_tags.items()))}`",
        "",
        "| # | File:line | Kind | Tags | Full normalized sentence |",
        "|---:|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for index, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
        normalized = " ".join(record["text"].split())
        normalized = normalized.replace("|", "\\|")
        tags = ", ".join(record["tags"])
        rows.append(
            f"| {index} | `{record['file']}:{record['line']}` | "
            f"{record['kind']} | {tags} | `{normalized}` |"
        )
    OUTPUT_MD.write_text("\n".join(rows) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"files={len(paths)}")
    print(f"records={len(records)}")
    print(f"counts={dict(sorted(counts.items()))}")
    print(f"rule_tags={dict(sorted(rule_tags.items()))}")
    print(f"syntax_tags={dict(sorted(syntax_tags.items()))}")
    print(OUTPUT_JSON)
    print(OUTPUT_MD)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    12	  // ==== values, the algebraic lists, and the scope heap =====================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= ".IntSeq" | iCons(Int, IntSeq)
    14	  syntax ValSeq ::= ".ValSeq" | vCons(Val, ValSeq)
    15	  syntax Str    ::= str(IntSeq)

    17	  // the iterable values, grouped under one sort (typing only — dispatch is <k>-cell)

    25	  syntax Val      ::= Int
    26	                    | Bool
    27	                    | "noneV"
    28	                    | Iterable
    29	                    | ref(Int)          // a heap object: <heap> holds its list(VS)
    30	                    | cellRef(Int)      // a closure cell: <heap> holds cellV(V)
    31	                    | closureVal(ParamNames, Stmts, Int)
    32	                    | typeV(String)     // a type object (int/str), resolved from the builtins frame
    33	                    | builtinV(String)  // a builtin function, resolved like any name (LEGB fallthrough)
    34	                    | boundMethodV(Val, String)   // a cooled Attribute: obj.method

    36	  syntax Parent   ::= "root" | parent(Int)

    44	  // ==== configuration =======================================================
    45	  // The builtins namespace is a real scope at reserved location -1 (the bottom of every
    46	  // chain; scopeLoc only allocates >=1, so -1 never collides). The module scope (loc 0)
    47	  // has it as parent, so an unbound name resolves there last — exactly LEGB. `int`/`str`
    48	  // resolve to their type objects; any local/global binding shadows them via normal lookup.
    49	  configuration
    50	    <k>       #loadAll($PGM:Module) </k>
    51	    <env>     0 </env>
    52	    <scopes>   0     |-> scope(.Map, parent(-1))
    53	              -1    |-> builtinsScope </scopes>
    54	    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    55	    <heap>    .Map </heap>
    56	    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    57	    <stack>   .List </stack>
    58	    <ret>     noRet </ret>
    59	    <exc>     NoExc </exc>
    60	    <exit-code exit=""> 0 </exit-code>

    62	  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
    63	  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
    64	  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
    65	  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
    66	  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
    67	  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
    68	  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
    69	  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
    70	  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]
    71	
    72	  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
    73	  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
    74	  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
    75	  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
    76	  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
    77	  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
    78	  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
    79	  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
    80	  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
    81	  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
    82	  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
    83	  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
    84	  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
    85	  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
    86	       <env> L:Int </env>
    87	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
    89	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    90	       [priority(40)]
    91	
    92	  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
    93	  // cell-bound names)
    94	  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
    95	  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
    96	  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
    97	  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
    98	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool isKwV(V)
   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]
   103	
   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
   109	  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
   110	  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
   111	  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)
   112	
   113	  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
   114	  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
   115	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>
   116	
   117	  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
   118	  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
   119	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
   120	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
   121	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
   122	
   123	  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
   124	  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
   125	  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
   127	  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>
   128	
   129	  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
   130	  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
   131	  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
   132	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
   133	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   134	       requires X in_keys(M)
   135	  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
   136	  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
   137	  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
   138	  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
   139	  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
   140	  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
   141	  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
   142	  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
   143	  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
   144	  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
   145	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
   146	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   147	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
   148	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
   149	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
   150	        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
   151	       [priority(40)]
   152	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
   153	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
   154	       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
   155	
   156	  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
   157	  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
   158	  rule builtinsScope
   159	    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
   160	                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
   161	                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
   162	                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
   163	                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
   164	                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
   165	                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
   166	                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
   167	                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
   168	                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
   169	                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
   170	                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
   171	                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
   172	                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
   173	                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
   174	                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
   175	                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
   176	                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
   177	                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)

   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)

   224	  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
   234	  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
   235	  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
   236	  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))

     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, …699 tokens truncated…#pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    81	        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    86	
    87	  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
    95	endmodule

    50	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), tuple(VS:ValSeq)) => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), list(VS:ValSeq))  => #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> Assign(TupleExpr(TS:Exprs), ref(H:Int)) => Assign(TupleExpr(TS), V) ... </k>
    53	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    54	       [priority(40)]
    55	  rule <k> #unpackSeq((T:Expr, TS:Exprs), vCons(V:Val, VS:ValSeq))
    56	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> #unpackSeq(TS, VS) ... </k>
    57	  rule <k> #unpackSeq(.Exprs, .ValSeq) => .K ... </k>
    58	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   122	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/comprehension.k — MPY-COMPREHENSION
     2	
     3	module MPY-COMPREHENSION
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     6	  imports MPY-LIST
     7	  imports MPY-CONTROLS
     8	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
     9	
    10	  // A comprehension is pure syntactic sugar
    11	  rule ListComp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors) => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    12	  rule GenExp(ELT:Expr, Gs:CompFors)   => Call(closureExpr(.ParamNames, compBody(Gs, ELT)), .Exprs)
    13	
    14	  syntax Stmts ::= compBody(CompFors, Expr) [macro]
    15	  rule compBody(Gs:CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    16	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), ListExpr(.Exprs)) compNest(Gs, ELT) Return(Name("$acc"))
    17	
    18	  syntax Stmt ::= compNest(CompFors, Expr) [macro-rec]
    19	  rule compNest(.CompFors, ELT:Expr)
    20	    => Assign(Name("$acc"), BinOp("+", Name("$acc"), ListExpr(ELT)))
    21	  rule compNest((CompFor(T:Expr, ITER:Expr, Fs:Exprs) GRest:CompFors), ELT:Expr)
    22	    => For(T, ITER, If(compGuard(Fs), compNest(GRest, ELT), .Stmts))
    23	
    24	  syntax Expr ::= compGuard(Exprs) [macro]
    25	  rule compGuard(.Exprs)             => Bool(true)
    26	  rule compGuard((F:Expr, Fs:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (F, Fs))
    27	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/dict.k — MPY-DICT
     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.
    12	
    13	module MPY-DICT
    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST
    18	
    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).
    20	  syntax Val ::= dictV(ValSeq, ValSeq)
    21	
    22	  // ==== DictExpr: {k: v, ...} literal. Eval each key then value, left to right, insert-with-dedup.
    23	  syntax KItem ::= #dictAcc(Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    24	                 | #dictKey(Expr, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)
    26	  rule <k> DictExpr(ES:Entries) => #dictAcc(ES, .ValSeq, .ValSeq) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #dictAcc(.Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq) => dictV(KS, VS) ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    29	        => K ~> #dictKey(V, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    31	        => V ~> #dictVal(KV, REST, KS, VS) ... </k>
    32	  rule <k> VV:Val ~> #dictVal(KV:Val, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)
    33	        => #dictAcc(REST, dPutK(KS, KV), dPutV(KS, VS, KV, VV)) ... </k>
    34	
    35	  // insert-with-dedup helpers (concrete Val key equality via ==K). [total] so buildFold over a dict is
    36	  // total (its #Ceil is #Top) — needed when a symbolic proof carries a built dict as a config value.
    37	  syntax Bool ::= dHasKey(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    38	  rule dHasKey(.ValSeq, _:Val)                => false
    39	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => true          requires A ==K K
    40	  rule dHasKey(vCons(A:Val, R:ValSeq), K:Val) => dHasKey(R, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
    41	
    42	  // dPutK: KS unchanged if K already present, else append K (keep-first-position).
    43	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutK(ValSeq, Val) [function, total]
    44	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => KS                                  requires dHasKey(KS, K)
    45	  rule dPutK(KS:ValSeq, K:Val) => valSeqConcat(KS, vCons(K, .ValSeq)) requires notBool dHasKey(KS, K)
    46	
    47	  // dPutV: parallel to KS — set the value at K's position if present, else append V at the end. The
    48	  // [owise] catch-all covers the degenerate mismatched-length case (never reached for a well-formed dict).
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= dPutV(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val, Val) [function, total]
    50	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)  => vCons(V, VR)
    51	       requires A ==K K
    52	  rule dPutV(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(B, dPutV(KR, VR, K, V))
    53	       requires notBool (A ==K K)
    54	  rule dPutV(_KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq, _K:Val, V:Val) => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq)) [owise]
    55	
    56	  // ==== dict methods ========================================================
    57	  // d.keys() -> a FRESH list object of the ordered keys (k-cell: it allocates).
    58	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(dictV(KS:ValSeq, _:ValSeq), "keys")), .Vals)
    59	        => #alloc(list(KS)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	
    62	  // ==== dict subscript READ: d[k] (assoc lookup; KeyError is out of subset) ==
    63	  rule applyIndexD(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KS, VS, K)
    64	  syntax Val ::= applyIndexD(Val, Val) [function]
    65	  rule <k> Subscript(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val) => applyIndexD(dictV(KS, VS), K) ... </k>
    66	       [priority(45)]
    67	
    68	  // ==== dict subscript-assign: d[k] = v (insert/update in place) =============
    69	  // Only for a LOCAL dict variable X (the current scope holds it). Reuses dPutK/dPutV.
    70	  syntax Val ::= dictSet(Val, Val, Val) [function]
    71	  rule dictSet(dictV(KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val) => dictV(dPutK(KS, K), dPutV(KS, VS, K, V))
    72	
    73	  // RHS evaluates first (Assign strictness), then the key. Dispatch on the scope
    74	  // value: a bare dict updates in the scope (dicts stay values); a ref (a heap
    75	  // list — or a heap dict later) writes the heap in place.
    76	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetK(String, Val)
    77	  rule <k> Assign(Subscript(Name(X:String), K:Expr), VV:Val) => K ~> #dsetK(X, VV) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    79	       <env> L:Int </env>
    80	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- dictSet({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ], _) ... </scopes>
    81	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool notBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    82	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dsetK(X:String, VV:Val) => #dsetV({M[X]}:>Val, KV, VV) ... </k>
    83	       <env> L:Int </env>
    84	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    85	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    86	  syntax KItem ::= #dsetV(Val, Val, Val)
    87	  rule <k> #dsetV(ref(H:Int), I:Int, VV:Val) => .K ... </k>
    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31

    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>

    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>

    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
